items.title: A pseudo-coherent complex over a local ring is determined up to isomorphism by the dimensions of its residue field fibres
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that a pseudo-coherent object of the derived category of a local ring is represented by a complex of free modules whose ranks are the dimensions of the residue field fibres, and that this complex is unique up to isomorphism (statement lines 19547-19563). The proof splits into existence and uniqueness: existence follows by pulling pseudo-coherence to the residue field, replacing the fibre by a complex with zero differentials and applying the lifting statement, while uniqueness is proved by choosing a map of complexes between two representatives and observing that its reductions modulo the maximal ideal are isomorphisms because the induced map on the fibres is one, whence each degree is an isomorphism (proof lines 19565-19591). The degreewise reduction argument is the technical heart of the uniqueness half. The counted span refers three times, twice to results of this chapter and once to a result of another chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
